summary: This section deals with a situation where a company plans to sell its shares or other securities to the public through another party. Any document used to make this public offer is officially treated as a prospectus. This means the document must follow the legal rules and carry the same responsibilities as a normal public offer.
points: Treats any document used to offer a company's allotted securities for sale to the public as a prospectus issued by the company.
Applies all legal rules regarding prospectus contents and mis-statements to these public offer documents.
Considers an allotment to be made with a view to public sale if the public offer happens within six months or if the company has not yet received full payment.
Requires the document to state the net amount of consideration received by the company and where the allotment contract can be inspected.
Allows a document offered by a company or firm to be signed by two directors or at least half of the partners.
example: Alpha Plastics Limited allotted securities to an investment firm with the plan that the firm would soon sell them to the public. Within two months, the investment firm issued a document offering these securities to the general public. Under the law, this document is treated as a prospectus issued by Alpha Plastics Limited. Therefore, all standard legal rules regarding prospectus contents and responsibilities for any mis-statements apply to this document, just as if the company had offered the shares directly to the public.

terms.meaning: Financial instruments like shares or debentures issued by a company.
An official document inviting the public to buy securities of a company.
Payment or value received in exchange for securities.

watch: Do not confuse this with a direct public issue, as this rule applies when securities are first allotted to an intermediary and then offered to the public.
